component.name: Composa
component.summary: Layer-based image editor for compositing and retouching

description.p: Composa is a layer-based image editor for compositing and retouching, with Photoshop-style tools and shortcuts. It is a from-scratch implementation of Compositor, Robbie Tilton's open-source macOS app.

ul.li: Layers with masks, clipping, blend modes, groups and layer effects
Selections: marquee, lasso, magic wand, object and subject selection, feathering
Brush, eraser, clone, heal, dodge, burn and sharpen, with pen pressure
Adjustments: levels, curves, hue and saturation, exposure, colour balance and more
Text layers, transforms, rulers, guides, grid and snapping
Opens Photoshop files and camera RAW; exports PNG, JPEG and WebP

description.p: An AI agent can drive the editor through a Model Context Protocol server, a Painterly filter turns a photo into a painting that is still that photo, letters of a text layer can have their own colors, saving writes in the background, sliders show their colors and can be reset, and Motion Blur's angle has a full-circle dial.

Photoshop Large Document files, editable Photoshop text, SVG import, a memory budget for the whole document, sliders you drag, scrub or type into, a dial for shadow angles, and a color picker laid out as Photoshop's.

The first stable release, and the first for Windows: an installer and a portable zip for x64 and arm64, with ImageMagick included so HEIC, AVIF, TIFF and camera RAW open without anything else installed.
The Camera Raw Filter, finishing filters, blur and noise adjustment layers, the Inner Glow effect, layer copy and paste, Image Trim, and a notice when a newer version is available.
The first release with downloadable packages for Linux.
